primarySource.paper: Pratt, Robles, Zaharescu, Zeindler, arXiv:1802.10521, Res. Math. Sci. 7 (2020) - full-text extraction 2026-11-06
primarySource.bindingEstimate: end of the Theorem 4.1 proof: 'The variable U is of size N1/(d h), thus when U appears there is a hidden h. The significance of the power of h being less than the power of U is that we need some positive power of h in the denominator at the end of the day so we can sum over h and not have it blow up. Since sum_{h|d^infty} G(h)/h^eps << (dT)^eps, we find that ... A*_{M,N1,N2} << (T^eps/d)(T^{1/2}N^{7/8} + N^{7/4}). Thus, taking N = T^{4/7-eps} is permissible.'
primarySource.dIdentity: d is a DIVISOR (h | d^infty) in the Type I/II bilinear decomposition with U = N1/(d h) - the 1/d factor is INTERNAL to the optimization whose endpoint is (7/4, 7/8); it is not the degree of the coefficient family and not a free parameter
primarySource.coefficientFamily: section 2/3.4/7: Lambda_k(n) := (mu * log^k)(n) (Lambda_1 = the usual von Mangoldt); the degree-D family (mu * Lambda_1^{*k1} * ... * Lambda_D^{*kD})(n), total truncation l = k1 + ... + kD contour variables; the mu^2-restricted variant agrees at l = 1 and is relaxed to the unrestricted form between Theorem 4.1's second and third error cases
primarySource.mainTheoremSetup: section 8: the 5/12 proof uses d = 1 (linear case only), truncation K = 3 (mollifier has polynomials P_1, P_2, P_3), theta = 4/7 - eps, R = 1.3036, degree-5 Q(x) = 0.490464 + 0.636851(1-2x) - 0.159327(1-2x)^3 + 0.032011(1-2x)^5, achieving kappa >= 0.417293962 > 5/12
primarySource.openQuestions: section 9 verbatim: item 3 'how one can increase the length of the Dirichlet polynomials without specializing the coefficients a_n too much'; item 4 'It would also be interesting to set d = 1 and analyze how a large truncation of l could yield terms from a higher degree d >= 2. What would be a good balance between the degree d and the truncation l?'

audit.leverIdentity: the d-l trade-off (section 9 item 4) acts on the MAIN TERM (the richness of the kappa optimization): for fixed d = 1, large l_1 expands (mu * Lambda_1^{*l_1})(n) into products of logs of distinct primes dividing n - the SAME term shapes that arise at degree d >= 2 - so large truncation mimics higher degree; this changes the main-term structure (more degrees of freedom for the polynomial Q -> better kappa), while the ERROR bound A* is UNIFORM in the family (the structure enters only via the separation reduction to bilinear Kloosterman sums)
audit.misreadingSealed: the 'make d large' reading of the 1/d factor is a MISREADING: d is a divisor length (h | d^infty) inside the bilinear decomposition; the (7/4, 7/8) endpoint already includes it, the h-U power constraint (h-powers strictly below U-powers, needed for the h-sum convergence), and the W = U^{1/4} balance - the proof's paragraph explains why the current extraction is FORCED by the structure
audit.wallLeverVerdict: as a proportion lever (kappa) the d-l trade-off is structurally blind to the sparse face (0285/0292 logic: proportion results cannot exclude a sparse off-line zero set); it adds NO new wall lever. The wall levers remain exactly the 0303 menu: L1 sharper bilinear Kloosterman estimate (changes 7/4 or 7/8), L2 new balance beyond the forced h-U constraint, L3 different decomposition/coefficient structure (section 9 item 3)
